articles.title: Where Is the Border? How Architecture Controls and Reimagines Mobility
articles.summary: The article examines the design of border entry corridors, focusing on how concrete walls, low ceilings, and minimal lighting shape the visitor’s experience. It highlights how such environments function to control, manage, and even reimagine the movement of people through design cues like a bulletproof glass window and an officer’s presence. The piece discusses the broader implications of architecture in regulating                                                                                mobility and identity at points of crossing.

articles.title: Casa Macahuite / Studio Font
articles.summary: Casa Macahuite is conceived as five intersecting planes—four vertical walls and a floating pergola—arranged in harmony with the surrounding sea and mountains. The architectural configuration creates intermediate shaded spaces that provide natural cross-ventilation and a continuous line of sight to the landscape. The design emphasizes a seamless integration of built structure and environment, achieving a balance between privacy and communal openness.

articles.title: "Promoting Another Way of Living Together": In Conversation with Cristina Gamboa of Lacol
articles.summary: At the UIA World Congress of Architects 2026, the discussion expanded beyond design կենտրոն to include governance and stewardship of housing. Cristina Gamboa, co‑founder of Lacol, contributed insights on alternative models of collective living that prioritize long‑term care and socio‑economic equity. The dialogue illustrated how architectural practices can shape community resilience and shared lifestyle choices.

articles.title: Cork House / Polysmiths
articles.summary: Polysmiths built a three‑bedroom home on an infill block in East London using cork and other pandemic‑era sustainable materials. The design leveraged locally available resources to create an eco‑friendly living space that maintained affordability and resilience. The project showcases how circular design principles can be implemented in dense urban settings.

articles.title: From Data to Digital Twins: Japan’s PLATEAU Project Offers Open-Access Models of More Than 250 Cities
articles.summary: Japan’s Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism spearheads Project PLATEAU, delivering open‑access 3‑D models of its 744 cities, including the 14 largest. The initiative fosters urban simulation, planning, and civic engagement through detailed digital twins that capture geographic diversity. The project underscores how data‑driven architecture can transform municipal policy and public transparency.

articles.title: An Architectural Language of Artificial Cooling: Shade, Mist, and Autonomy
articles.summary: The洔ºerrículo festival in Logroño created full‑scale installations that explored artificial shading, misting, and autonomous cooling technologies as a response to urban heat. Participants engaged with the city’s microclimate, turning everyday streets into experimental public spaces. The project demonstrates how rapid‑ prototyping in architecture can generate adaptable, climate‑responsive designs.

articles.title: Gabonsa Pavilion / Hochschule Kaiserslautern University of Applied Sciences
articles.summary: Students from Kaiserslautern University collaborated with Innsbruck collectives to design a temporary pavilion for the Gabonsa Music Festival. The pavilion, located at the Rossau Recreation Centre, serves as both a performance space and a communal gathering point. The project illustrates how educational institutions can partner with artists to create temporary, context‑specific architectural solutions.

articles.title: The House of Green Court / andblack design studio
articles.summary: Situated in Ahmedabad, the House of Green Court adapts historic courtyard typologies to organize a multi‑generational family into individualized yet cohesive units. The design modulates privacy and communal spaces to meet evolving inhabitant needs, with a strong emphasis on climatic adaptation. The project showcases how traditional forms can inform contemporary sustainable house planning.

articles.title: Luohu Library and Youth Activity Center / Shenzhen ΓιαφΑᚳ Design + iDEA
articles.summary: Situated at the intersection of pristine mountains and layers of urban fabric, the LuTours Library and Youth Activity Center performs a hybrid role between public learning and ecological experience. The building uses natural permeability to blend the built environment with the surrounding landscape. It highlights how early‑stage library design can foster community engagement while protecting natural resources.

articles.title: Blue Bottle Coffee Harajuku Cafe / TEKI Design
articles.summary: TEKI Design redefined urban space in Harajuku by creating a permeable passageway that provides a slice of sky between dense high‑rise buildings. The cafe’s interior emphasizes natural light and flexible seating to resonate with the ever‑shifting Harajuku culture. The design illustrates how minimalistic interventions can transform narrow city corridors into public open spaces.

articles.title: Mami Dan Temple of Toligbé Cultural Center / Maison Bignon Sossou
articles.summary: Maison Bignon Sossou integrated architecture as a vessel for preserving and transmitting living African heritage through the Mami Dan Temple of Toligbé. The design honours traditional ceremonial elements while providing a functional cultural centre that accommodates present‑day community needs. The project exemplifies how contemporary architecture can serve as a living archive for cultural practice.

articles.title: Mimado Restaurant / García de Alba +raiser Arquitectos
articles.summary: Mimado Restaurant annotations a double‑height commercial space into a warm, layered ambience highlighted by Art‑Deco references and extensive greenery. The interior design juxtaposes textured materials such as green येथे tile, white oak, and fluted glass to create a distinct yet cohesive dining experience. The project illustrates how curated material palettes can transform a vibrant space with botanical elements into a memorable customer journey.

articles.title: CTA shelters annexe in Vietnam beneath curved roof to "evoke the sensation of being Erinnerung in a cave"
articles.summary: CTA studio designed a large, open living annexe beneath a sweeping curved roof for a client’s home in Phu My near Ho Chi Minh City. The design employs scale‑shaped shingles and a circular roof opening to create a sense of being within a cave while maintaining natural ventilation. The project demonstrates how subtle Routed forms can produce a distinctive spatial experience in contemporary residential architecture.

articles.title: "Human refrigerator" provides escape from deadly heatwaves
articles.summary: SDRS produced a human‑sized stainless‑steel fridge, the Do Hiemon Box, to protect individuals from extreme heat wave conditions. The box features vents that direct chilled air to provide a cooling vault for one person during scorching summer temperatures. The product represents a novel approach to personal thermal comfort amid evolving climate realities.

articles.title: Manchester Digital Campus slated to become No 10 North
articles.summary: AtkinsRéalis has designed a new digital campus in central Manchester that is projected to host the office of No 10 North, extending the ինatural reach of the UK’s political leadership. Built on brownfield land in a vibrant suburb, the facility aims to support digital infrastructure and innovation. The project aligns with Britain’s strategy to promote regional governance through technology‑focused physical spaces.

articles.title: RSHP unveils tripartite Shanghai skyscraper informed by historical laneways
articles.summary: RSHP completed One Shanghai, a 186‑metre mixed‑use skyscraper inspired by Shanghai’s intricate laneway network. The triple‑segmented form reflects historical pathways, integrating contemporary function with the city’s legacy. The project underscores how contextual referencing can shape modern high‑rise designs in a global metropolis.

articles.title: FSB relaunches 1986 Dieter Rams door handle with "effortless grip"
articles.summary: Franz Schneider Brakel revived Dieter Rams’ 1986 FSB 1138 door handle, replacing its original plastic parts with an all‑metal construction for enhanced durability. The new design maintains the iconic minimalist line whilst improving user ergonomics and longevity. This update exemplifies the endurance of classic industrial design principles in contemporary product iterations.

articles.title: Sander seating island encourages reclining from all angles
articles.summary: Objekte Unserer Tage launched the Sander seating island, a versatile furniture piece that follows in the company’s sculptural marshmallow‑sofa tradition. The island’s central backrest offerstoggle support from both sides, allowing users to recline from any direction. The design reinforces the brand’s focus on ergonomic adaptability within a playful aesthetic.

articles.title: Public Art Company tels studio gives its own office a "muppets on acid" interior
articles.summary: Public Art Company’s LA studio design incorporates a curtain system that partitions areas for clustered collectibles, providing a colorful, playful environment for its team. The office’s interior embraces improvisational art elements akin to a psychedelic puppet show. The project highlights how creative agencies can reflect their identity through vibrant studio spaces.

articles.title: LEGO’s Star Trek Turns 60 Into 1,701 Pieces of Pure Nostalgia
articles.summary: LEGO released the Star Trek set commemorating the franchise’s six‑decade legacy, offering over 1,700 pieces to recreate iconic moments from The Next Generation. The set is a nostalgic homage to fans, blending detailed miniature modeling with the play value flagship brand is known for. The launch demonstrates LEGO’s continued capacity for cultural preservation through modular design.

articles.title: The 5 Best Tiny Homes of July 2026
articles.summary: The July 2026 roundup presents five compact yet well‑engineered tiny homes that prioritize efficient use of space and sustainable construction. Each design addresses common challenges raft: reducing footprint while maintaining livability through innovative layouts. The article highlights how tiny houses can be both affordable and environmentally conscious.

articles.title: Pocketbyte: The Modular Open Source PDA Nobody Knew They Still Wanted
articles.summary: Pocketbyte emerges as an open‑source modular PDA, reviving_forepast interest in physical electronics while embracing contemporary open‑source culture. The device reverses smartphone dominance by offering modular upgrade paths and tangible tactile controls to users seeking a more functional, design‑focused device. This project showcases a niche yet meaningful answer to the decline of standalone PDAs.

articles.title: The €169 Portable Mechanical Keyboard That Makes the Mouse Unnecessary
articles.summary: This affordable portable mechanical keyboard provides a full‑size experience on a compact chassis, integrating a mouse function via a robotic arm for a fluid point‑and‑click workflow. Its mechanical keys deliver satisfying tactile feedback while the built‑in mouse reduces the need for a separate peripheral, ideal for mobile users. The design illustrates a clever convergence of keyboard and mouse technologies within a singlestipble.

articles.title: The $55 Hub That Charges Your iPhone, Gives Your MacBook Ports, and Powers a 4K Display Together
articles.summary: This low‑cost hub combines charging and connectivity, offering iPhone and MacBook support alongside a 4K display output within a single unit. Its compact design enables versatile use for mobile workflows and home entertainment setups. The product emphasizes affordability and all‑in‑one functionality for power users.

articles.title: 5 Tiny Homes and Fold-Out Cabins Built to Move Wherever You Go
articles.summary: This feature spotlights five adaptive tiny homes and fold‑out cabins designed for mobility and instant deployment. Each structure employs modular construction techniques that allow it to be transported or stored in limited space, offering residents a flexible living solution. The article showcases how portable architecture can reinterpret the concept of home ownership.

articles.title: Field Notes Just Made Notebooks That Look Good Enough to Eat
articles.summary: Field Notes’ latest release focuses on edible‑looking notebooks that blend food‑friendly design with practical notebook usage. The pages feature texture and motifs that mimic edible surfaces, challenging conventional notebook aesthetics. This playful iteration illustrates how packaging design can incorporate sensory elements beyond functionality.

articles.title: This 2,200‑Piece LEGO Moth Kit Is Basically Taxidermy Without the Guilt
articles.summary: The new LEGO moth kit boasts 2,200 pieces, reconstructing a delicate butterfly within a plastic frame, mimicking calendars or miniature wearables. The kit invites builders to appreciate intricate natural patterns while avoiding animal exploitation. Culturing a collectibles culture, the product demonstrates how LEGO subcommunities can exist outside mainstream themes.

articles.title: This PlayStation Controller Sofa Was Built for Co‑Op Gaming Marathons
articles.summary: The PlayStation controller sofa transforms a sofa into a gaming station by embedding controller sockets and padded seating for comfortable gameplay. It features integrated charging points and ergonomic cushioning for long‑term co‑op sessions. The product illustrates a blending of furniture and interactive entertainment to support gaming communities.

articles.title: OHLAB Just Built a Home That Runs on Mallorca’s Sun
articles.summary: OHLAB’s Casa Óculo,tsx designed a circular roof opening to harvest sunlight for the building’s photovoltaic system, converting solar energy into household electricity. The home incorporates a minimalist façade that harmonizes with the Mallorca landscape while prioritizing energy autonomy. The project underscores how architecture can leverage sunlight as a primary power source, creating fully renewable dwellings.

articles.title: Flatbike's Accessories Let You Fold Your Bike Flat for Storage
articles.summary: Flatbike introduced the THINstem product, a stem that allows traditional bicycle handlebars and pedals to lie flat for convenient vehicle and storage transport. By reconfiguring geometry, the stem maintains standard riding dynamics while enabling easy stowage. This innovation demonstrates how bike Loe permitting solutions can redirect cycling toward urban commuters’ needs.
